name: Operation Azure Echo
description:
Scenario Overview

The fictional threat actor "Azure Echo" initiates the attack by sending a spear‑phishing email with a weaponized Office document to several finance analysts. The document drops a BITS Jobs script (T1197) that downloads a containerized payload (T1609) onto the endpoint. Once executed, the malware creates a new scheduled task (T1543) for persistence and adds a privileged service account (T1098) to maintain long‑term access.

Using stolen credentials, the actors perform token impersonation (T1134) and signed binary proxy execution (T1216) to evade detection while they enumerate the environment (T1681, T1682). Keylogger modules capture user input (T1056) and cloud storage objects are accessed for valuable documents (T1530). Collected data is packaged, encoded (T1132), and exfiltrated over HTTPS with size‑limit checks to avoid throttling (T1030) and through a legitimate web‑service API (T1567). Command and control traffic is hidden behind port‑knocking sequences (T1205) to blend with normal traffic.

Your Mission

  • Correlate the initial spear‑phishing alert with the BITS Jobs execution log.
  • Identify the scheduled task and new service account used for persistence.
  • Detect token manipulation and signed binary usage indicative of stealth techniques.
  • Map the reconnaissance activity to the victim identity and network discovery techniques.
  • Trace the encoded C2 beacon and stop the port‑knocking channel.
  • Prevent exfiltration by blocking the encoded payload and terminating active data transfers.
  • Provide remediation steps to remove persistence mechanisms and reset compromised credentials.
